tasks.short: Review published technical material and recommend changes to content, scope, format and production.

steps.what: Collect published editions, current specifications, reader feedback and production requirements.
Annotate outdated instructions, terminology problems, omissions and inconsistencies.

loop.input: Published passages, corresponding approved specifications, style guide and term list.
loop.output: Rule violations and possible substantive discrepancies, each linked to source passages.
loop.check: Validate version identifiers and citations; distinguish exact mismatches from uncertain interpretations; writer reviews findings.
loop.stop: One comparison pass and one correction pass per section; unresolved or unsupported findings enter manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Rules catch terminology and version differences; changed technical meaning requires interpreting prose.

steps.what: Decide which issues justify changes in scope, content or format.
Write revision recommendations with examples and reasons.

loop.input: Writer-selected priorities, approved source passages and revision brief template.
loop.output: Proposed changes with supporting sources, examples and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Require sources for technical claims; check terminology; writer confirms recommendations preserve technical meaning.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims remain questions; writer completes unresolved recommendations.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates organise the brief but cannot explain varied prose changes or their consequences.

steps.what: Discuss revision scope and production options with technical and publication owners.
Approve the revision brief and assign follow-up work.

tasks.design: A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} assembles version-linked material from the {DOCS}, {CMS} and {HELPDESK}; deterministic checks and bounded comparisons produce a cited review pack. The writer chooses priorities and reviews a drafted brief in the {DOCS}; approval through the {WORKFLOW} creates work items in the {PROJECT}. Technical changes require technical-owner acceptance before publication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source versions and feedback were scattered, while rules covered only part of substantive review. Integration and maintenance often cost more than occasional manual reviews.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing style checks, version metadata and bounded text comparisons can support review. AI-assisted coding can reduce implementation effort, but the local benefit needs measurement.
tasks.still_hard: Determining whether instructions remain safe and complete requires technical expertise. Poor source control and unusual print or binding constraints still create expensive exceptions.
tasks.human_edge: The writer weighs reader needs, technical consequences and production constraints, and notices omissions that comparison checks miss.

ambition.what: Monthly revision-priority review for the active manual catalogue.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time collecting editions and more time testing priorities with technical owners. With delegated authority, they can reorder low-risk editorial work; technical scope and publication approval remain with their owners.

reach.task: Plan a revision queue across related publications.
reach.learn: Editorial prioritisation, content dependencies and release planning.
Print specifications, production constraints and cost trade-offs.

evidence.claim: Repeatable terminology and house-style checks can support the mechanical part of review.
A vendor case reports fewer translation edits and shorter reviews; it does not establish this task's savings.
Version-linked comparisons and approval routing are feasible with controlled records and interfaces.

assumptions: Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, informed by the supplied judgement-heavy priors.
Published manuals and approved specifications have identifiable versions.
Build ranges cover a small pilot; shared components overlap with other tasks.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply. Personal feedback is minimised and model access is controlled.
Access estimates include employee consultation where national rules require it; approval waiting time may exceed build effort.
unknowns: How reliably published editions map to approved specifications.
Who may approve editorial, technical and production changes.
Whether reader feedback contains personal or confidential information.
Available interfaces and the applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: How many substantive discrepancies does a bounded comparison miss on previously reviewed manuals?
Does reviewing the generated pack take less time than the current review method?
new_work: Review cited discrepancies and reject false positives.
Route uncertain technical changes to technical owners.
Maintain source mappings, style rules and brief templates.
Monitor comparison quality and integration failures.

tasks.short: Choose photographs, drawings, diagrams and charts that explain technical material.

steps.what: Read the draft and identify passages needing illustrations.
Search stored assets and request missing illustrations from technical colleagues.
Inspect candidate illustrations for technical accuracy, clarity and relevance.
Select illustrations and specify crops, annotations and placement.
Check usage rights, approved versions and production suitability.
Attach cleared assets and placement instructions to the publication draft.

tasks.design: Configure an asset catalogue in the {DOCS} with equipment identifiers, versions, rights and production metadata. Filters assemble candidates and deterministic checks flag missing permissions or unsuitable files; the writer selects the explanatory image and clears exceptions. The {WORKFLOW} packages cleared assets and placement instructions for the desktop publisher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Asset folders often lacked consistent identifiers, version records and reusable permissions. Choosing the clearest explanation remained a visual and technical judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: Metadata forms, file checks and document packaging already exist as standard capabilities. AI-assisted coding makes small validation and handoff extensions cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: A plausible illustration can show the wrong equipment variant or hide a hazard. Rights interpretation, technical validation and explanatory choices still need people.
tasks.human_edge: The writer chooses what the reader must see and recognises misleading perspective, missing context and unsafe crops.

ambition.what: Task-indexed illustration catalogue for technical publications.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time hunting files and more time checking whether images explain the task. They can curate reusable editorial selections; new technical depictions still require technical-owner validation.

reach.task: Brief a diagram that explains an operating sequence.
reach.learn: Visual hierarchy, perspective, annotation and diagram conventions.

reach.task: Specify accessible illustrations for digital manuals.
reach.learn: Text alternatives, contrast and responsive image behaviour.

evidence.claim: Metadata filters, file validation and asset packaging can reduce search and handoff work.
Selecting technically accurate explanatory images remains dependent on visual and domain judgement.

assumptions: The target uses existing approved images; it does not assume reliable generation of equipment illustrations.
Step shares reflect the supplied selection-heavy priors; search savings depend on metadata quality.
Build ranges exclude a large historical asset-cleanup project.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant; identifiable people in photographs require appropriate handling.
Access effort includes employee consultation where national rules apply; no employee-performance monitoring is proposed.
unknowns: Whether assets have searchable equipment identifiers and approved versions.
Completeness of rights records and any restrictions on crops or annotations.
Supported catalogue features and interfaces in the current {DOCS}.
research_questions: Can metadata filters retrieve useful candidates without semantic image matching?
Which file checks catch the most recurring production defects?
new_work: Tag new assets and repair incomplete catalogue records.
Resolve missing permissions and obsolete equipment variants.
Review catalogue usefulness with writers and designers.

tasks.short: Agree technical specifications and publication scope with customers, suppliers and internal technical owners.

steps.what: Collect existing specifications, customer requests and previous publication decisions.
Prepare questions about users, technical limits, publication scope and unresolved requirements.

loop.input: Selected source documents and a fixed requirements checklist.
loop.output: Cited background summary and questions about missing or conflicting requirements.
loop.check: Validate source references; separate known requirements from assumptions; writer selects the questions.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; missing sources produce explicit questions; writer handles unresolved conflicts.
loop.why_not_simpler: A checklist supplies headings but cannot identify contradictions in varied customer and technical prose.

steps.what: Arrange the discussion and share the agenda with participants.
Discuss intended use, technical constraints and publication scope with stakeholders.
Write the scope brief, decisions, open questions and assigned actions.

loop.input: Writer's discussion notes, provisional scope and approved source documents.
loop.output: Scope brief distinguishing agreed decisions, proposals and open questions.
loop.check: Link requirements to notes or sources; reject inferred agreement; writer confirms owners and commitments.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; ambiguous agreement remains open; writer completes unresolved wording.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text notes need interpretation to distinguish commitments from suggestions; templates alone cannot do that.

steps.what: Confirm technical commitments and send the scope brief for stakeholder acceptance.

tasks.design: A controlled job assembles relevant records from the {DOCS}, {CRM} and {EMAIL}, then a bounded loop drafts a cited agenda. People conduct the discussion; another bounded loop turns their notes into a scope brief in the {DOCS}. The {WORKFLOW} routes technical approval, sends the approved acceptance request and records stakeholder responses before scope is treated as accepted.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements arrived through conversations and inconsistent documents. Scheduling and paperwork were separate from the human work of clarifying needs and negotiating scope.
tasks.enabler_now: Calendar workflows and structured scope forms handle coordination. Bounded drafting can organise supplied notes without assuming that ambiguous statements are agreements.
tasks.still_hard: Stakeholders may disagree or leave essential constraints unstated. Technical commitments, customer acceptance and sensitive supplier information require deliberate human handling.
tasks.human_edge: The writer asks follow-up questions, recognises hesitation and negotiates a scope people can actually deliver.

ambition.what: Operator comprehension briefing before publication scope is finalised.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends more of the week clarifying reader needs and less assembling agendas and minutes. They can lead requirements discovery; technical commitments and customer acceptance keep their existing decision owners.

reach.learn: Neutral questioning, sampling and separating observations from assumptions.

reach.task: Define publication audiences and intended outcomes.
reach.learn: Audience segmentation and prioritising competing stakeholder needs.

evidence.claim: A writing trial found faster professional drafting; it did not test technical-scope negotiation.
Source-linked agenda and scope drafting are plausible bounded uses of models, subject to local validation.
Scheduling, approval routing and acceptance tracking can use configured workflows.

assumptions: The conversation-heavy priors are retained; preparation and paperwork are separate opportunities.
The pilot uses written notes and does not require recording participants.
Records can be retrieved using known project and customer identifiers.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply; customer, employee and supplier data require controlled processing.
Access effort includes employee consultation where national rules apply; elapsed approval time can be longer.
unknowns: Who can commit to technical specifications and accept publication scope.
Whether external stakeholders require a particular acceptance process.
Confidentiality restrictions on customer and supplier documents.
Available access to relevant records and applicable national consultation requirements.
research_questions: Does scope drafting preserve the distinction between proposals and agreed commitments?
Which agenda questions reveal missing requirements before the main discussion?
new_work: Verify meeting notes, commitments and action owners.
Resolve conflicting requirements and track outstanding acceptance.
Maintain scope templates, retrieval filters and access permissions.
Review model errors and prevent inferred agreement from entering approved records.

tasks.short: Help arrange technical text and illustrations into publication-ready layouts.

steps.what: Collect approved text, illustrations, layout templates and production specifications.
Import content and apply styles in the {OTHER} publishing tool.
Adjust page breaks, tables and illustration placement in the {OTHER} publishing tool.
Review the rendered proof for readability, missing content and production defects.
Package the approved layout and assets using the {OTHER} publishing tool.

tasks.design: Configure reusable styles and import mappings in the {OTHER} publishing tool, with approved sources assembled from the {DOCS}. Deterministic preflight checks compare rendered content with source text and flag overflow, broken references and unsuitable assets. The writer handles layout exceptions and approves the proof before an internal production package is generated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inconsistent source formatting and exceptional tables or diagrams limited template reuse. Manual proof checking compensated for weak content structure and export validation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing publishing templates and export controls handle repeatable layout. AI-assisted coding can cheaply add content-completeness checks and connectors without requiring a model to design pages.
tasks.still_hard: Dense diagrams, multilingual expansion and unusual tables need visual judgement. Rendering can change across fonts and environments, so technical instructions must be checked in the actual output.
tasks.human_edge: The writer keeps warnings, steps and illustrations together so readers can understand and follow the instruction.

ambition.what: Accessible digital manual edition from the same approved content.

tasks.altitude: The writer spends less time applying styles and more time resolving difficult reading sequences and layout exceptions. They gain capacity to specify reusable templates; final production release retains its existing approver.

reach.task: Maintain reusable publication templates and production presets.
reach.learn: Typography, pagination, font handling and print preflight.

reach.task: Design navigation for an accessible digital manual.
reach.learn: Semantic structure, keyboard navigation and responsive reading layouts.

evidence.claim: Templates, paragraph styles, import mappings and export presets can automate repeatable layout work.
Deterministic checks can flag missing assets, broken references and content differences, while visual proof review remains necessary.

assumptions: The supplied human classification does not prevent automation of repetitive style application and packaging.
The {OTHER} publishing tool supports reusable templates and controlled export.
Source text and assets are already approved; this task does not author new technical instructions.
Build ranges cover one publication family and output format; the ambitious digital edition requires additional work.
GDPR and the EU AI Act apply where relevant. Access effort includes consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Current publishing-tool capabilities and supported import formats.
Consistency of source styles, fonts and illustration references.
Required output formats, accessibility requirements and production presets.
Who approves layout proofs and authorises production release.
research_questions: Which template rules remove the most repeated layout adjustments?
Can completeness checks catch omitted warnings and table rows without excessive false alarms?
new_work: Maintain templates, import mappings and export presets.
Inspect rendered proofs and resolve exceptional tables or diagrams.
Update preflight rules when production requirements change.
Verify regenerated packages after source, font or rendering changes.

role.altitude: The technical writer's week shifts toward explaining difficult procedures, validating meaning and resolving stakeholder disagreements. Explicit delegation can expand editorial prioritisation and template decisions; technical commitments and publication release retain named human owners.
reach: Editor: plan related revisions using content dependencies and reader impact.
Graphic designer: brief technically accurate diagrams and explanatory sequences.
Desktop publisher: maintain templates and assess production constraints.
Market research analyst: interview operators and test comprehension.
Web and digital interface designer: shape accessible digital manuals.
skills_to_grow: Source provenance and technical change validation.
Reviewing bounded model outputs and maintaining exception rules.
role.ambitious_version: Offer a publication-readiness service that joins version-linked sources, operator comprehension checks, reusable illustrations and validated outputs. Measure fewer misunderstood instructions and faster verified revisions before expanding the service.
